source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Thank you for sharing this newest iteration. The hierarchy is heading in the correct direction again, but I believe we should reset the way we review the work to prevent further backward steps.

Going forward, I want every presentation to use a consistent format.

Unless I explicitly ask for a change, the following relationships must stay locked:
Hero V — Preserve the currently agreed hierarchy and the percentage of elevation of the right arm. This continues to serve as the master geometry for the entire system.
Second V — Build it proportionally from the Hero V while retaining the agreed relationship above the cap height of the surrounding letters. It must function as a restrained echo of the Hero V and should never compete with it.
É Accent — Use an exact duplicate of the Hero V's right arm, ending at precisely the same peak height and carrying over identical terminal geometry.
Presentation

For all subsequent iterations, please show two versions of every option.

Left column

Hero V peak height
Alphabet cap height
Second V peak height

Right column

Show the exact same artwork without any reference lines.

This format lets me assess the design on its own while verifying that the hierarchy has not changed.

New Assignment: Terminal Exploration

The hierarchy now seems close enough that I want the next phase to concentrate solely on the terminal language.

Leave every other element identical and develop six clearly distinct terminal treatments for the Hero V only.

I do not want six minor variations on one answer. Each treatment should represent a genuinely different design philosophy.

The following five directions may be useful for guiding the exploration:

1\. Soft Architectural

Draw inspiration from carved limestone, travertine, or premium architecture.

Remain geometric
Use subtly eased corners
Feel warm without looking rounded
Convey quiet confidence
2\. Sculpted

Approach the termination as though it had not been cut.

Instead, imagine it had been carefully sculpted.

Subtle transitions
Refinement that is nearly invisible
Hand-finished instead of manufactured
Elegant restraint
3\. Faceted Gemstone

Take cues from a gemstone cut with precision.

Several subtle planes
Refined, not sharp
Luxurious without appearing decorative
Crisp while still polished
4\. Cast Bronze

Envision molten bronze being poured into a mold.

Keep the geometry precise
Allow the edges to soften naturally through casting
Make it feel less mechanical
Timeless and enduring
5\. Bespoke Furniture

Look to museum-quality cabinetry or furniture made by artisans.

The edge should appear deliberately broken
Engineered without ever becoming harsh
Sophisticated craftsmanship
Understated luxury
6\. Your Interpretation

Please also create one concept based entirely on your personal interpretation.

Considering everything we have developed together during the past several weeks, I want to see where your own design instincts take the work. Surprise me with the solution you feel expresses the VELLVÉ identity most effectively.

I am not seeking a vector that is merely softer.

What I want is a different sense of material quality.

Rather than reading as the endpoint of a line, the terminal should resemble the treated edge of an heirloom object.

It should feel:

Architectural
Refined
Quiet
Luxurious
Timeless
Precision-crafted

It must not feel:

Calligraphic
Rounded
Decorative
Fashion-oriented
Aggressive or sharp

After we establish the correct terminal language for the Hero V, apply it directly to the É accent and proportionally to the second V.

Thank you.

value_updates.alphabet_height_relationship: Retain the agreed relationship above the cap height of the surrounding letters while building the second V proportionally from the Hero V.
value_updates.right_endpoint_elevation: Derive the second V's right-arm elevation proportionally from the Hero V's agreed relationship while preserving its established restrained rise above the alphabet.
